r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding:
PASS, WITH A MATERIAL FINDING on THE ONE THING. All five "Also verify" items hold up under
independent attack; the corpus-shape trap is real, bigger than the crew's own evidence showed,
and worth reporting even though it does not sink the gate.

=== THE ONE THING: corpus-shape trap ===

The crew's own admission is accurate: superCoolSpaceSim (0 .py files) was a null test, so only
f1Brainz exercised the F9 trap (~75% test code). I found the trap fires on a corpus already IN
HAND -- this repo's own real, already-built map/INDEX.md -- and confirmed it in isolation with
two synthetic shapes.

REAL EVIDENCE, no synthesis needed (map/INDEX.md, fresh build this run): this repo's own
`tests` package is 50 modules / 2769 entities = 74.3% of the corpus's 3728 entities -- the SAME
proportion F9 named as the trap. It is a completely FLAT directory (every module is
`tests.test_foo`, two dotted segments). The tier predicate `len(m.split("."))>=3` never fires
for a single one of its 50 modules, so `## tests` renders as 50 undifferentiated `- [...]`
bullets with ZERO subheadings -- read it yourself: `map/INDEX.md` lines 89-140. This is the
exact flat-list failure mode the gate exists to fix, unaddressed, on the crew's own flagship
corpus, in the single bucket holding three-quarters of the repo. The crew's own
g4_tier_shape.md evidence only measured tier-1 sizes for constellation-skills (12/54, 49/905,
50/2769) and never looked at tier-2 behavior on this corpus at all -- if they had, they would
have found this.

SYNTHETIC CONFIRMATION, isolating the mechanism (`.agent-work/issue-456/evidence/
g4_reviewer_synth_corpora.py` + `.txt`, built into scratch temp dirs, nothing tracked touched):

  Shape A -- one flat package, 30 modules, zero nesting (the pytest-default layout: everything
  in one directory, no subpackages -- this is what `tests/` above IS, isolated from f1Brainz's
  mixed structure). Result: `## flat (31 modules, 30 entities)` followed by 31 loose bullets,
  0 `###` headings. Tier 2 provides no benefit whatsoever for this real, common shape.

  Shape B -- loose top-level modules, no packages at all (named explicitly in the handoff as a
  shape to try). Result: TIER 1 ITSELF degenerates. `BY_PKG` keys off `m.split(".")[0]`, so
  when every module has exactly one dotted segment, every module becomes its own "package."
  The `## packages` overview -- whose whole design rationale, stated in `top_index`'s own
  docstring, is "bounded by how many top-level packages the corpus has, never by how many
  modules" -- becomes a 30-line, one-package-per-module list, a 1:1 restatement of the module
  list it sits above. That docstring claim is FALSE for this shape. The crew's own evidence doc
  states "none is 'N buckets of one' (superCoolSpaceSim correctly reports nothing to route, not
  N empty headings)" -- but superCoolSpaceSim (0 modules) cannot exercise "N buckets of one" at
  all; it can only ever produce the single "no mappable modules found" line. Shape B is the
  actual "N buckets of one" case and the claim does not hold for it.

VERDICT ON THE SHAPE: both are REAL, not pathological. Shape A is this repo's own `tests/`
directory and the default pytest layout used across the ecosystem. Shape B is a small
script-bag repo with no package structure -- also common (single-purpose tool repos, ML
training scripts, most tutorial/demo repos). Neither is contrived to break the code; both are
ordinary layouts a code_map user will actually point this at.

Is this a blocker? I judge NOT, for three reasons: (1) the tier remains DERIVED, not TUNED --
it does not fabricate structure that isn't there, it honestly reports "nothing to group,"
which is what the crew's own docstring claims for the flat case (true) even though the
docstring's SEPARATE bound claim about tier 1 is false for shape B; (2) no test and no close
criterion asserts the tier eliminates the flat-list problem for EVERY shape -- the close
criterion is "derived, not tuned, shape reported per corpus," which holds; (3) nothing crashes,
corrupts, or produces a misleading/wrong index -- it produces an honest, if unhelpfully
granular, one. This is a real gap in the gate's stated purpose ("ROUTE, not list") for a
common corpus shape, filed as a triage candidate below, not a blocker.

=== Routing judgment (cold read of map/INDEX.md) ===

Read map/INDEX.md as a cold reader (fresh build, this run). It DOES route for `evals` (3 real
subpackages, clean) and partially for `scripts` (2 real subpackages surfaced, ~40 loose scripts
readable in one screen) -- genuine improvement over a flat list. It does NOT route within
`tests`, the dominant bucket (see above) -- there it is exactly the flat list the gate exists
to replace, just with one extra summary line above it. Net judgment: a real, measurable
improvement for corpora/packages with actual nesting (this repo's evals/scripts, f1Brainz's
src/), and a no-op for the flat/loose case -- which happens to be the single largest bucket in
the crew's own flagship corpus.

=== tc31 attack, with relocations the implementer did not choose ===

Implementer's own RED evidence: moved an ENTITY page cross-module (`pkg.callee:target.md`,
`pkg.callee/` -> `pkg.far/`). I ran two different relocations against a fresh real-corpus
build (`.agent-work/issue-456/evidence/g4_reviewer_tc31_attack.py` + `.txt`):

Attack 1 -- a MODULE page (not an entity page): moved `scripts.code_map.discovery/INDEX.md`
into `scripts.code_map.cli/`. check exit 1, `FAIL page-location-matches-content: 1`, naming
`scripts.code_map.cli/discovery-relocated-INDEX.md: titled module 'scripts.code_map.discovery',
expected at scripts.code_map.discovery/INDEX.md`. All other 6 checks stayed green (isolated).

Attack 2 -- an ENTITY page moved into a SUBDIRECTORY of its OWN correct module (same module,
wrong parent, not a cross-module move): moved `scripts.code_map.discovery/discover_corpus.md`
to `scripts.code_map.discovery/nested/discover_corpus.md`. check exit 1, `FAIL
page-location-matches-content: 1`, naming the exact page and expected dir. Other 6 checks
stayed green.

Both attacks confirm the check is genuinely load-bearing and not vacuous: it fires precisely
on the relocation, nothing else in the suite masks or duplicates it, and it fires on relocation
shapes the implementer's own reproducer never tried (module-page move; same-module-wrong-subdir
move). tc31 is genuinely CLOSED.

=== Threshold re-grep ===

`git diff 0e63f208..HEAD -- scripts/code_map/render.py scripts/code_map/checks.py` shows
exactly ONE new numeric comparison in the entire diff: `len(m.split(".")) >= 3`
(render.py, inside `top_index`). No new slice, sort-then-truncate, or count threshold anywhere
else in the diff (checked the full added-lines diff directly, not a targeted grep that could
miss a slice). Pre-existing numeric comparisons elsewhere in render.py (`largest_5 =
sizes[:5]` in the render_report.json diagnostic, `len(v) > 90` truncating a docstring preview,
`len(group) > 1` for page_file's case-fold collision naming) are all UNCHANGED by this diff and
are not part of the tier/routing path -- confirmed by diff, not by memory of the file's
pre-existing shape.

=== Non-falsifier label ===

`test_top_index_lists_a_loose_module_directly_with_no_subheading` -- confirmed the label is
accurate. `git show 0e63f208:scripts/code_map/render.py`'s old `top_index` never emits a `###`
heading under any input (no such code path existed pre-gate), so `assertNotIn("### pkg.other",
text)` was trivially true before this gate for ANY fixture -- consistent with "passed unchanged
before and after." It is NOT a check that cannot fail post-gate, though: read the fixture
(`_make_nested_subpackage_repo`, `pkg.other` has no sibling module sharing "pkg.other" as a
3+-segment prefix) and traced `module_group_key`/`subpkgs` by hand -- if a future edit grouped
every module under itself (or otherwise widened what counts as "grouped"), `pkg.other` would
pick up a `### pkg.other` heading and this test would go red. Correctly labeled a regression
guard, not a falsifier, and not tc29/tc38's "check that cannot fail" defect.

No blocker from this item. Filed as triage candidate below.

pure ASCII with no :<line> (scanned all 3840 built pages, zero hits); the non-falsifier is
correctly labeled a regression guard, not a check-that-cannot-fail (traced by hand: it WOULD
catch a regression that widened grouping to swallow loose modules). Full suite reproduced
independently: 1772 passed, 2 skipped, 672 subtests, 0 failed (310.98s). Fresh build+check:
7/7. All named exclusions (INDEX collision, OWN_MODULE_NAMED_MUTATION, entity_symbol_join
independence, no :<line>) reconfirmed directly, untouched by this diff. Fowler pass 12/12
absent, rail exit 0.

THE MATERIAL FINDING: the corpus-shape trap is real and bigger than the crew's own evidence
showed. Only f1Brainz genuinely exercised critic F9's trap in the crew's own proof (super
CoolSpaceSim was an admitted null test). I found the trap ALREADY PRESENT, unexamined, in the
crew's own flagship corpus: this repo's own `tests/` package is 50 modules / 2769 entities =
74.3% of the corpus -- the same proportion F9 named -- and is completely flat, so the tier
predicate never fires for it: zero subheadings, 50 undifferentiated bullets, exactly the

This does not block: the tier remains derived, not tuned (it reports "nothing to group"
honestly rather than fabricating structure), no close criterion promises uniform routing
across every shape, and nothing crashes or misrepresents the corpus. But it means the gate's
own stated purpose ("the top index must ROUTE, not list") is only partially achieved, and is
